For an allocation a+b=2s, translating each transverse section into u⊥ identifies its Minkowski midpoint with a subset of the actual K_s. Brunn–Minkowski applies to these nonempty compact sections even if one has zero (d−1)-volume. Gardner's stated Theorem 4.1 explicitly allows this. Its threshold signs at bases −1 and +1 are α and −α, respectively.

Section-root concavity holds on each actual closed projection interval. At a support endpoint interpolation toward a fixed interior height gives the stated lower limit, and compactness gives the upper limit by neighborhoods of the endpoint section. Consequently the maximum is attained on the compact allocation set. Convexly combining maximizing allocations shows concavity of the maximum root, so the profile is measurable and Fubini integrates it.

The centered replacement balls have radii proportional to the section roots and give compact convex bodies by continuity and concavity. Zero-volume support sections become points. The axial means and volumes agree with the sheared endpoint profiles, and the other centroid coordinates vanish by reflection.

At each fixed midpoint height the sum of centered transverse balls is a centered ball of radius equal to the average. The maximum contains every other allocation. With K the exact Minkowski midpoint of these replacements, h is therefore the actual section volume for every height, so equality holds for every α using the same bodies.
